events.venue: Studio 34, 4522 Baltimore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19143
events.description: Bartram’s Garden is the oldest surviving botanical garden in North America. Located in an urban neighborhood, it is a gem of nature that may seem incongruous to first-time visitors. In the 1720s, botanist John Bartram built a stone house overlooking the Schuylkill River, and began farming the 107 acres of land around it. In his spare time, Bartram followed his interest in native plant species and traveled widely collecting plants and seeds from th northern shores of Nova Scotia to the southern tip of Florida. He founded a botanical garden on the five acre plot between his house and the river and developed a nursery that sold native plants and served as a base for correspondence with other botanists on both sides of the Atlantic. events.title: Let Freedom Ring
events.venue: Cherry Street Pier, 121 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
Paul Ramírez Jonas’ monumental artwork plays the song “My Country ‘Tis of Thee” in its entirety—all but the final note. Participants must pull a lever to ring the last note on a 600-pound bell at the base of the sculpture to complete the song, a metaphor for how we can work together as a society to fulfill the unfinished promises of our nation’s founding. This artwork promotes civic engagement by providing a public site to speak, listen, and learn from one another, and to bring people together to imagine a more inclusive future that embraces the complexities of our past.

events.title: Being Present with Art: Welcoming Change
events.venue: The Barnes Foundation, 2025 Benjamin Franklin Pkwy, Philadelphia, Pe 19130
events.description:
As summer shifts into autumn, we invite you to slow down through mindful engagement with art. Seasonal transitions heighten our awareness of change—in the natural world, in our routines, and within ourselves. This workshop, held in the Barnes galleries, offers a space for greater awareness of these changes.
Developed by Roksana Filipowska, Being Present with Art is a method that integrates mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) meditation with works of art and pedagogical exercises such as close looking and writing. Together, these practices have been shown to lower stress and encourage deeper observation, self-reflection, and a renewed sense of belonging.

events.title: Volta
events.venue: SideQuest Theater
events.description:
When Wren arrives at the Mariposa Hotel, she is certain something bad has happened, and she will fix it by finding her sister Lottie. Yet nothing at the Mariposa Hotel moves or functions in quite the way Wren expects. Staff pops out of walls, doors lead to museums where memories stand like sculptures, people call loved ones from other dimensions, and she keeps just missing Lottie. And throughout, a writhing, pulsing, shifting mass invites her to join blissful oblivion. As Wren searches for Lottie, she revisits her life in fits and bursts, finding tenderness, bitterness, loss, and celebration in equal measure.
VOLTA is a play about love's lasting power after the death of the self.

Aiden Ankli

events.title: Bartram’s Garden Photo Exhibit at Studio 34
events.venue: Studio 34, 4522 Baltimore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19143
events.description: Bartram’s Garden is the oldest surviving botanical garden in North America. Located in an urban neighborhood, it is a gem of nature that may seem incongruous to first-time visitors. In the 1720s, botanist John Bartram built a stone house overlooking the Schuylkill River, and began farming the 107 acres of land around it. In his spare time, Bartram followed his interest in native plant species and traveled widely collecting plants and seeds from th northern shores of Nova Scotia to the southern tip of Florida. He founded a botanical garden on the five acre plot between his house and the river and developed a nursery that sold native plants and served as a base for correspondence with other botanists on both sides of the Atlantic. Desperate to save the world and restore Christmas cheer, they must now turn to the one person who can still be haunted for good:
a dumbass stoner named me.

Can a nobody change the world?

events.title: The Holy Fool
events.venue: The Gym at Impact Services
events.description:
This world premiere dance-theater piece uses cinematic style to explore familial bonds, love, and heartache.
Mother makes dinner. Daughter sets the table. One empty chair. A knock at the door. Expecting someone? Back to dinner. You made a mistake. Everyone’s watching. The bills pile up. The job’s never done. Another disaster. And your face—it’s older. The cameras are rolling. The Fool is laughing. You’re doing just fine.
Through the eyes of an American family, The Holy Fool examines the toll of aging, grieving, and growing up in a culture where normativity is the most valuable currency. events.title: The Suppliants
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Third Floor
events.description:
Inspired by Aeschylus' "The Suppliants" - one of the oldest surviving plays in the Western canon - this new ensemble-driven performance reimagines an ancient story through the lens of Appalachian folklore.
What begins as a tale from the distant past slowly unfolds into something far more immediate: a meditation on refuge, belonging, and the choices communities make when confronted with outsiders seeking safety.
Blending elements of Greek tragedy, folk traditions, movement, and devised performance, the work explores how stories travel across generations and why certain myths refuse to disappear.

events.title: Let Freedom Ring
events.venue: Cherry Street Pier, 121 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
Paul Ramírez Jonas’ monumental artwork plays the song “My Country ‘Tis of Thee” in its entirety—all but the final note. Participants must pull a lever to ring the last note on a 600-pound bell at the base of the sculpture to complete the song, a metaphor for how we can work together as a society to fulfill the unfinished promises of our nation’s founding. This artwork promotes civic engagement by providing a public site to speak, listen, and learn from one another, and to bring people together to imagine a more inclusive future that embraces the complexities of our past.

events.description: Combining Shakespeare's language with events from Cousar’s picaresque life, with its absurd calamities and unexpected glories, Avalanche of No will interweave DJ culture, the life of a real-life porter, custody battles, physicalized images of Jean-Michel Basquiat, and 3-card monte into a frank display of bravura storytelling. It will lead audiences into a confrontation of dream with reality, of destiny with real-world circumstance, all filtered through a lens of Afropessimism - experienced by many, recognizable by all. events.title: Bad Clay
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Project Space
events.description: In this work, I am weaving text from performance scores and personal poetry to create a solo performance entitled BAD CLAY, an experience that experiments with the intersection of Ceramics and Performance. Live ceramic construction (both hand building and at a potter's wheel) collides with dance, clay, and ceramic sculpture to expand the limits of 2 bodies into one: clay and flesh. Driving the work are questions around migration and immigration (where do bodies come from and what are they destined for?), intimacy (how can bodies connect through clay?), and performance art (what are all of the expressions of clay and performance that already exist and how can we further their possibilities?). events.description:
Pack Your Baggage, The Future of Queer Art Awaits!
Welcome to the Bearded Ladies’ Hairport, an interactive installation & performance series built on 16-years of accumulated baggage from a queer cabaret company devoted to art, care, mess, and community. While you’re waiting for a flight that may never take off, unpack your baggage and rifle through some of ours. You may recognize something as your own, or find something you never knew you were carrying.
Made for anyone who has ever lost a bag, gotten stuck, or missed a (metaphoric) flight, this trans(formational) installation asks: how do you know it’s time to move on when you don’t know where you’re going?

events.title: Bartram’s Garden Photo Exhibit at Studio 34
events.venue: Studio 34, 4522 Baltimore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19143
events.description: Bartram’s Garden is the oldest surviving botanical garden in North America. Located in an urban neighborhood, it is a gem of nature that may seem incongruous to first-time visitors. In the 1720s, botanist John Bartram built a stone house overlooking the Schuylkill River, and began farming the 107 acres of land around it. In his spare time, Bartram followed his interest in native plant species and traveled widely collecting plants and seeds from th northern shores of Nova Scotia to the southern tip of Florida. He founded a botanical garden on the five acre plot between his house and the river and developed a nursery that sold native plants and served as a base for correspondence with other botanists on both sides of the Atlantic. events.title: John Miller Giltner’s A Christmas Carol
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Found Spaces
events.description:
Turmoil and heavy ass shit has come to the three spooky ghosts made famous by Charles Dickens Christmas Carol. As greed and corruption rule in our time, their attempts to haunt billionaires fall on deaf ears. Their warnings bounce off private islands, ketamine therapy, and underground bunkers.
Desperate to save the world and restore Christmas cheer, they must now turn to the one person who can still be haunted for good:
a dumbass stoner named me.
And here’s the whole freaking deal: if I don’t change, Christmas is more dead than Kristi Noem with a new puppy.

events.title: Echoes of Dammām
events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description:
Echoes of Dammām is a multimedia storytelling performance that follows fragmented stories gathered around dammām, a ritual drumming practice from Bushehr, a port city in southern Iran.
On stage, live narration moves alongside projected video, field recordings, and layered sound. Drums, voices, images, silence, and memory appear in fragments, tracing how grief, resistance, and the struggle for freedom can live inside sonic and bodily practices. Drawing from ethnographic fieldwork in Bushehr, the performance does not tell a single linear story. Instead, it creates an intimate audiovisual space where ritual mourning, Black musical heritage, histories of circulation and loss, and personal memory echo through one another.

This event originally codenamed "Operation Hummingbird" is commonly referred to as The Night of the Long Knives. While you’re waiting for a flight that may never take off, unpack your baggage and rifle through some of ours. You may recognize something as your own, or find something you never knew you were carrying.
Made for anyone who has ever lost a bag, gotten stuck, or missed a (metaphoric) flight, this trans(formational) installation asks: how do you know it’s time to move on when you don’t know where you’re going?

In the 1720s, botanist John Bartram built a stone house overlooking the Schuylkill River, and began farming the 107 acres of land around it. In his spare time, Bartram followed his interest in native plant species and traveled widely collecting plants and seeds from th northern shores of Nova Scotia to the southern tip of Florida. He founded a botanical garden on the five acre plot between his house and the river and developed a nursery that sold native plants and served as a base for correspondence with other botanists on both sides of the Atlantic. events.title: The Holy Fool
events.venue: The Gym at Impact Services
events.description:
This world premiere dance-theater piece uses cinematic style to explore familial bonds, love, and heartache.
Mother makes dinner. Daughter sets the table. One empty chair. A knock at the door. Expecting someone? Back to dinner. You made a mistake. Everyone’s watching. The bills pile up. The job’s never done. Another disaster. And your face—it’s older. The cameras are rolling. The Fool is laughing. You’re doing just fine.
Through the eyes of an American family, The Holy Fool examines the toll of aging, grieving, and growing up in a culture where normativity is the most valuable currency. A thrilling ghost story unfolds in a dreamlike visual landscape scored by a hypnotic blend of trumpet, percussion and synthesizers. Co-Directed by Ninth Plan

events.description:
“All Below” is a multimedia devised two-person theatre performance that exists in a pocket universe between clown, cosmic horror, and 19th century poetry. Also, there are puppets.
Drawing inspiration from Carlo Rovelli’s book on quantum physics, The Order of Time, as well as the magical realism of Jorge Luis Borges, the performance maroons two Victorian explorers outside of the flow of linear time as their minds attempt to grapple with the impossible and unknowable in their exploration(s) of the phantom island of Saxemberg.

events.description:
Turkish-Colombian-American performer, Izzy Sazak, takes the audience on a wild ride; unpacking the awkward beauty of growing up mixed, caught between two empires worth of daddy issues and messy history. Tuzluk lovingly deconstructs the myth of the neo-liberal hero-man; mixing geopolitics with a hilarious, heartfelt and fast paced examination of identity and inheritance. Tuzluk deftly weaves together a collage of memory and fantasy to tell a story of making peace with the one thing none of us get to choose- one’s fortune.
* Tuzluk: turkish for “salt shaker”, and the colloquial name for the popular children’s paper fortune teller game.

events.title: Cicada Stories
events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description:
When considering this work, I was drawn to the idea of an anti-performance, creating something that would be unknown to all until it was physically uttered. This work continues my research and examination of a performer’s relationship to viewership and audience. With risk and remix at the forefront, Cicada Stories explores chance, choice, and neutrality in a performance setting. How do our expectations differ as we take on the roles of performer or audience member? How do we impact the performance space just by being? What if our actions taken weeks ago were impacting the now, played out on stage? Through constants and variables, this work becomes less of a show and more of an experiment, a game that is played by all.

events.description:
My Carmilla centers Laura, an isolated young woman growing up in 1870s New England. Reflecting years later, she invites the audience into a world of religious doctrine, watchful eyes, and isolation.

events.title: Days of Awe
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Third Floor
events.description:
A year after her mother’s death, a poet in recovery moves home to Philadelphia to get a divorce and start a new life. Set during the ten days from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, this solo show blends poetry, storytelling, and chutzpah into a lyrical reckoning with grief, the inheritances we carry, and the possibility of reinvention after rupture.
Told with equal parts reverence and irreverence, Days of Awe draws on family history and Jewish ritual to ask how we can carry loss without surrendering desire.

events.title: Handle with Care
events.venue: Athenaeum of Philadelphia
events.description:
Handle with Care is a theatre performance in a box. No actors, no technicians. Just a box. And you.
A box is mailed to the theatre.
The instructions are clear:
Invite a group of people, on a specific date, at a specific time.
Let the audience take their seats.
Place the box at the centre of the stage.
The audience is waiting.
And then an audience member stands up and opens the box.
The show has started.
In Handle with Care, the audience is in control. The artists provide the structure; you shape the experience. Choose your role—take the lead or observe as others make choices. Together, you create something special: a shared experience filled with reflections on time, transience, and togetherness. And don’t worry—there are no wrong choices. F

By weaving together star quilts, geometric abstraction, and materials that carry cultural memory, she creates a visual language that honors ancestral knowledge while pushing contemporary art forward. The name “Stephen Girard” looms large over Philadelphia today, both because of the fortune he left to the city upon his death in 1831, and because of the many Civil Rights controversies surrounding his namesake school, Girard College, in the twentieth century.

events.description: Can you find yourself by being someone else? Spencer Boyce has been an Elvis Tribute Artist since he was six years old. events.title: soft spot
events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description: "soft spot" is a dance work for the child within us, uninhibited and open to the potential of everything. Vyette Tiya and her collaborators use the language of movement to explore tenderness, vulnerability, and intimacy — a glance that turns into a grasp, a tease that turns into a collision, a game that tumbles into freefall. Framed through a series of vignettes, "soft spot" asks: how do we wish to be seen? Who can see us? How do we remain tender in a world that hardens us?

This is a show about failing hard, falling down, and getting back up and joining the dance... because THAT'S SHOW BIZ, BABY!

events.description: Oleanna is an uncomfortably relevant play that explores the intricate interplay of gender, authority, control, and education. Witness the deeply personal and profoundly affecting dialogues between a university professor and his student as they struggle to truly understand one another. The academic setting becomes a crucible where assumptions are challenged and communication breaks down. Written in 1992 in response to the Anita Hill-Clarence Thomas hearing, Oleanna invites audiences to reflect on their own perspectives, assumptions, and values. events.description:
A unique interdisciplinary experience where, performers, visual artists, and creative boundary-pushers from completely different worlds collide with the audience in real time.
One Night Only exists once, lives fully, and then it's gone. You won't find a recording of last night's show. You won't be able to catch the next one and get the same experience. events.venue: The Sound Lounge, 1700 N Front Street, Philadelphia, PA 19122
events.description:
Join us in welcoming our newest Friday night resident, Nine of Wands to our rotating weekly Friday night residencies at TSL every weekend from 8-11!
At the core of every paradigm rests faith in dogma, faith that underneath layers of complexity lie static, foundational truths. These beliefs act as guiding forces on our individual journeys.
All the Way Down is a residency conceptualized by Nine of Wands; a nod to the mythological idea of the world resting on an infinite number of turtles. It is a playful, musical invitation to explore our axioms with acceptance and curiosity, to push up against what is believed to be static and open towards unity, kindness, and mutual understanding.
Until then, it’s turtles all the way down.

Welcome to the Bearded Ladies’ Hairport, an interactive installation & performance series built on 16-years of accumulated baggage from a queer cabaret company devoted to art, care, mess, and community. events.title: The Holy Fool
events.venue: The Gym at Impact Services
events.description:
This world premiere dance-theater piece uses cinematic style to explore familial bonds, love, and heartache.
Mother makes dinner. Daughter sets the table. One empty chair. A knock at the door. Expecting someone? Back to dinner. You made a mistake. Everyone’s watching. The bills pile up. The job’s never done. Another disaster. And your face—it’s older. The cameras are rolling. The Fool is laughing. You’re doing just fine.
Through the eyes of an American family, The Holy Fool examines the toll of aging, grieving, and growing up in a culture where normativity is the most valuable currency. A thrilling ghost story unfolds in a dreamlike visual landscape scored by a hypnotic blend of trumpet, percussion and synthesizers. Co-Directed by Ninth Plan

events.venue: Lil' Filmmakers Inc.
events.description:
“All Below” is a multimedia devised two-person theatre performance that exists in a pocket universe between clown, cosmic horror, and 19th century poetry. Also, there are puppets.
Drawing inspiration from Carlo Rovelli’s book on quantum physics, The Order of Time, as well as the magical realism of Jorge Luis Borges, the performance maroons two Victorian explorers outside of the flow of linear time as their minds attempt to grapple with the impossible and unknowable in their exploration(s) of the phantom island of Saxemberg.

events.description:
Paul Ramírez Jonas’ monumental artwork plays the song “My Country ‘Tis of Thee” in its entirety—all but the final note. Participants must pull a lever to ring the last note on a 600-pound bell at the base of the sculpture to complete the song, a metaphor for how we can work together as a society to fulfill the unfinished promises of our nation’s founding. This artwork promotes civic engagement by providing a public site to speak, listen, and learn from one another, and to bring people together to imagine a more inclusive future that embraces the complexities of our past.

events.description:
Handle with Care is a theatre performance in a box. No actors, no technicians. Just a box. And you.
A box is mailed to the theatre.
The instructions are clear:
Invite a group of people, on a specific date, at a specific time.
Let the audience take their seats.
Place the box at the centre of the stage.
The audience is waiting.
And then an audience member stands up and opens the box.
The show has started.
In Handle with Care, the audience is in control. The artists provide the structure; you shape the experience. Choose your role—take the lead or observe as others make choices. events.description:
Uncover the tragedy and heroism of Philadelphia’s 1793 epidemic on a guided tour through historic Christ Church Burial Ground.
Step back and confront the reality of Philadelphia's most devastating epidemic on our Yellow Fever Tour at Christ Church Burial Ground. In late summer 1793, a terrifying fever swept through the nation's capital, taking thousands of lives and sending panic through the streets.
This guide-led tour leads you through the grounds where both victims and key figures of the outbreak. As you walk among the headstones, you will explore 18th-century medical theories, the breakdown of civic life, and the remarkable stories of care and courage that emerged during a citywide crisis.

events.description:
How can we communicate when words fail? If the need is desperate enough, can we escape language and still be understood?
The Voynich Manuscript is a real, 15th century codex written in an unknown language. Alongside 240 pages of text in a unique alphabet, it depicts people bathing in strange contraptions, botanical details of unknown plants, and astrological star charts unlike any on earth. Some scholars suggest it is a complex hoax, yet text analysis and information theory suggest the letter and word frequency match those of a real language.

events.description: EVE IN PARADISE is a one-person play. It is a loose stage adaptation of John Milton’s Paradise Lost, a pointed commentary on Paradise Lost, and at its core, a memoir. The actor plays Eve. She is a biblical troublemaker, a seventeenth century puritanical ideal, and a 21st century intersectional feminist, who has lost her faith. The audience finds Eve embodying the epic poem and cutting it with scenes from her own life. Turmoil and heavy ass shit has come to the three spooky ghosts made famous by Charles Dickens Christmas Carol. As greed and corruption rule in our time, their attempts to haunt billionaires fall on deaf ears. Their warnings bounce off private islands, ketamine therapy, and underground bunkers.
Desperate to save the world and restore Christmas cheer, they must now turn to the one person who can still be haunted for good:
a dumbass stoner named me.

I don’t know.

events.title: Handle with Care
events.venue: Athenaeum of Philadelphia
events.description:
Handle with Care is a theatre performance in a box. No actors, no technicians. Just a box. And you.
A box is mailed to the theatre.
The instructions are clear:
Invite a group of people, on a specific date, at a specific time.
Let the audience take their seats.
Place the box at the centre of the stage.
The audience is waiting.
And then an audience member stands up and opens the box.
The show has started.
In Handle with Care, the audience is in control. The artists provide the structure; you shape the experience. Choose your role—take the lead or observe as others make choices. MEAT CUTE is a bloody double-feature of two short plays that explore themes of the body, mind, and heart as meat. One play, MEAT PLAY, by Grace Stewart Gardner, is an exploration of the corruption of the modern American meat industry through the story of one worker, Bailey, who has just been assigned to begin their six months of employment on the Killing Floor. Studies show that the longer one spends working on the Killing Floor, where employees are expected to slaughter over 2,000 animals per day, the likelihood of committing a violent crime increases. events.title: Zombied
events.venue: Yellow Bicycle Theater
events.description:
What happens when your body falls apart? And when those parts follow you, waiting for–something? Do you listen to their grievances? Or scream until they leave? Do they ever leave? ZOMBIED is a gothic supernatural thriller about the fight to defend one thing we all think we deserve: our own bodies.
Queer and disabled people often find their relationships to their bodies irreparably shaped by the negative perceptions of monsters, and at the same time feel comforted by monstrous characters. ZOMBIED is a meditation on this tension, drawing from many of the class literary and gothic monsters we are all familiar with.

With Love From Ella is a powerful one-woman theatrical experience that celebrates the extraordinary life of the legendary Ella Fitzgerald. Through music, storytelling, and heartfelt performance, the production follows Ella's remarkable journey from hardship and uncertainty to becoming one of the most beloved voices in history.

After 250 years, Thornton Wilder's Our Town is considered America's greatest play.
So what's the problem?
Well, plenty as it turns out.

The slow pace, no plot or high stakes, the bare stage, mimed props and archetype characters. 21st century criticism is easy and obvious. And even queer theory has serious issues with Wilder and his character SIMON STIMSON.

With risk and remix at the forefront, Cicada Stories explores chance, choice, and neutrality in a performance setting. How do our expectations differ as we take on the roles of performer or audience member? How do we impact the performance space just by being? What if our actions taken weeks ago were impacting the now, played out on stage? Through constants and variables, this work becomes less of a show and more of an experiment, a game that is played by all.

Does it compensate through heightened senses elsewhere? Is somatic sensitivity amplified as a result of quieting distractions channeled through eyes and ears? events.description:

His grandfather wasn't terminally ill. He wasn't suffering from depression. A longtime leader in the right-to-die movement, he spent decades advocating for the idea that people should have the right to choose when and how they die. Using dance, poetry, and visual art as mediums and their body as the instrument, Kendall transposes their experience medically transitioning into an evening length dance performance that emphasizes how all humans know the feeling of their own bodies hurting them, physical limitations, or feeling disturbed by their reflection.

events.title: Zombied
events.venue: Yellow Bicycle Theater
events.description:
What happens when your body falls apart? And when those parts follow you, waiting for–something? Do you listen to their grievances? Or scream until they leave? Do they ever leave? ZOMBIED is a gothic supernatural thriller about the fight to defend one thing we all think we deserve: our own bodies.
Queer and disabled people often find their relationships to their bodies irreparably shaped by the negative perceptions of monsters, and at the same time feel comforted by monstrous characters. ZOMBIED is a meditation on this tension, drawing from many of the class literary and gothic monsters we are all familiar with.

events.title: Account
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Project Space
events.description: You come in and sit down and I tell you my complete financial history while scrolling through my debit and credit card purchases and pulling up my bank accounts, then you tell me what class I am. Thank you in advance for your help. It's a financial confessional that includes, shame, fraud, generational bag fumbling, and unproductive leftist angst.

events.title: Girls Gotta Eat
events.venue: Fat Moon Restaurant and Karaoke
events.description:
Rose and Sacha are hungry gals singing for their supper at Fat Moon Restaurant and Karaoke. Equipped with microphones, props, and questionable boundaries, they'll spend one hour attempting to earn enough tips to buy themselves dinner. Expect songs, dances, monologues, crowd work, and other acts of public ambition or public humiliation.
Part karaoke night, part variety show, part performance experiment, the evening draws inspiration from guerrilla art, porous boundaries between audience and performer, and the belief that everyday is a spectacle. Admission is a drink or food item. The value of their work is up to you. Drop in, drop out, stay for one Alanis, maybe bounce when the Boss comes on!!

events.title: Ascension Death March
events.venue: Studio 34, 4522 Baltimore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19143
events.description:
Ascension in stilettos. Strip-clown theology.
A mop becomes a cross. A pole becomes a tomb. Low art gets crucified.
Ascension Death March is a darkly funny dance-theater ritual exploring the brutal cost of chasing transcendence. Moving between physical theater, clown, strip-club aesthetics, ritual, and confessional monologue, Lu Anima wrestles publicly with transcendence, suffering, and the impossible task of figuring out which way is up.
The piece spirals through virtuosic spectacle, spiritual delusion, ambition, collapse, and the aching desire to become something greater.

events.title: First in the Hearts
events.venue: Yellow Bicycle Theater
events.description:
After 250 years, Thornton Wilder's Our Town is considered America's greatest play.
So what's the problem?
Well, plenty as it turns out.
The main criticism of the play is the idealized view of small-town America. The theatre complaints are legendary. The slow pace, no plot or high stakes, the bare stage, mimed props and archetype characters. 21st century criticism is easy and obvious. It's all WASP, with no diversity, it's sexist and heteronormative. Act One regaling the history of the town never mentions that Grover's Corners is on Pennacook land, part of the Abenaki nation. And even queer theory has serious issues with Wilder and his character SIMON STIMSON.

events.description:
In a forgotten corner of a nonprofit theater—somewhere between a prop closet and a spiritual crossroads—two employees find themselves tasked with an impossible mission: free the ghost haunting the space.
Their only tool?
The complete works of August Wilson.
